readme.html:
Casely: free AI test case generator for Claude

The spec is a PDF, and TestRail wants your team's columns.

Casely reads the requirements, you approve one test plan, and it returns test cases in your format, a Postman collection for API specs, and the gaps it found in the spec.

For manual QA engineers and QA leads who import cases into TestRail, Qase, Zephyr or Xray.

429 installs from the Claude plugin directory · 85/100 on a public benchmark · MIT

In Claude Code, paste this prompt instead:

Install the Casely plugin from https://github.com/JohnWayneeee/casely-qa-skill

Watch it work

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/57f086c4-ec92-4a60-bc58-a00cc9757ee0

The problem

You were hired to find bugs, and your week goes into writing test cases.

Requirements land as unstructured PDFs. Projects rename the columns, so you remap them each sprint. One module takes two days to document, and then the TestRail import fails because the headers don't match.

How it works

Attach your files and say what you need:

"Here are the requirements for the Payments module and two example test cases my team writes. Give me test cases for the refund flow."

Casely runs five phases in that same conversation:

Phase What happens
Intake Reads your PDF, DOCX or XLSX attachments, a Jira issue or epic, or a Confluence page. No parser, no OCR setup
Style guide Copies the column structure and tone from your example file, and can save it so you attach it only once
Test plan Proposes coverage, flags holes in the spec, then waits for your OK
Generate Writes the cases using boundary values, decision tables and negative paths
Export Builds one Excel file (or a UTF-8 CSV) your TMS imports in a single pass, plus a Postman collection when the requirements describe an API. /casely:run then walks the UI cases in a browser

You only get interrupted once, at the plan. Adjust the scope, drop a module, add negative cases, or say "go".

AI test case generation: a chat prompt vs Casely

Prompt in a chat Casely
Reads PDF, DOCX, XLSX requirements ✅ ✅
Uses your team's columns, order and ID scheme ➖ if you describe them each time ✅ copied once, saved for next time
Flags gaps and contradictions in the spec before writing ➖ if you ask ✅ in the plan
Waits for your approval of the coverage plan ❌ ✅
Boundary values, decision tables, state transitions ➖ varies ✅ part of the plan
One Excel file TestRail imports in one pass ❌ you format it ✅
Runnable Postman collection for API specs ❌ ✅
Reads a Jira issue or Confluence page ➖ you copy-paste it ✅ Atlassian connector
Arabic, Korean and other non-Latin text survive the export ➖ unchecked ✅ round-trip tested
Walks the cases in a browser and reports pass/fail ❌ ✅ /casely:run in Claude Code
Bug report from a trace ID in your team's format, data masked ➖ you paste and redact logs ✅ /casely:bug
Price your AI plan your AI plan, Casely itself is free (MIT)

Tested against a benchmark

The repo ships a fintech wallet spec with five planted defects (a vague "processed quickly", a limit that contradicts a worked example, an undefined "verified status" and more), boundary rules, a state machine and a five-condition decision table, plus a 100-point rubric. The first full run scored 85/100: 33 cases, all nine team columns in order, one workbook with no rejected case. The misses were two of the five planted gaps; the rules that catch them are now part of the skill. Details and the rubric: benchmark/README.md.

The export has its own test: tests/test_export_roundtrip.py writes Arabic and Korean cases with commas, quotes, an escaped pipe and line breaks to XLSX and CSV, reads both back and compares every cell, the row count and the column count. Run it with python -m unittest discover tests.

Jira, Confluence, and a browser run

Requirements from Jira or Confluence. The plugin ships Atlassian's official remote MCP server (https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp). Say "write test cases for PAY-142" or paste a Confluence link; the first time, Atlassian's own sign-in page opens and you approve access. No API token goes into a file or the chat. Casely reads the issue, its acceptance criteria and linked issues, and treats them like an attached spec. Name an epic or a sprint and Casely lists its stories and asks which to cover. The issue key can go into a requirement column, so you can filter the imported cases by story.

Read only. Casely never creates, edits or comments on anything in Jira or Confluence. A rule in a prompt is not a lock, so grant read access only: an Atlassian admin can limit the server to read and search, and in Claude Code a permissions.deny block removes the write tools. Copy the block from references/connectors.md.

Attach your example once. After the first run Casely offers to save your team's style as casely-style.md (.casely/style.md in Claude Code): headers, order, ID scheme and the last ID used, with real data replaced by placeholders. Next time it reads the file instead of asking for the example. On claude.ai, add the file to your Project knowledge.

Run the cases in a browser. In Claude Code, after an export:

/casely:run https://staging.example.com

Casely walks each UI case through the Playwright MCP server, records pass, fail or blocked, saves a screenshot for every failure and writes run/run_report.md. Connect Playwright once: claude mcp add playwright -- npx @playwright/mcp@latest. API cases stay with Newman.

Bug reports from a trace ID. In Claude Code:

/casely:bug 4f2a9c1e

Casely reads the event through your monitoring MCP server (GlitchTip, Sentry, or your company's own), or from logs you paste when you have no access, and writes one bug report in your team's fields: title, steps, expected and actual result, environment, trace link, a short log excerpt. Tokens, emails, user ids and IPs are masked. A failed case from /casely:run works too: /casely:bug WD-014. Attach your team's bug examples once and Casely saves the format. It never files the bug or touches the event: you file it. On claude.ai and Cowork, just ask for a bug report.

CSV for trackers that want it. Ask for CSV and the export adds all_test_cases.csv, UTF-8 with a BOM, so Excel and TestRail keep non-Latin text intact.

API requirements get a collection you can run

When the spec names endpoints (a path and a method, an OpenAPI file, curl examples, status codes, an auth section), Casely says so in the plan and, once you approve, exports the API-level cases as a Postman collection alongside the Excel file.

exports/
├── all_test_cases.xlsx                          # every case, your columns
├── casely_api_collection.postman_collection.json  # the API cases as requests
├── casely_api_environment.postman_environment.json # every variable, empty
└── casely_api_collection_README.md              # import, fill in, run, read results
  • Everything environment-specific is a variable. {{baseUrl}}, {{authToken}}, entity ids. Fill them in once and the same file runs against dev, staging, or CI. The value a case is actually testing (amount: 50001) stays literal, because that is the point of the case.
  • No credentials in the file. The build fails on anything shaped like a JWT or a secret key, so the collection is safe to commit next to the test cases.
  • Assertions come from the expected result. Status code, response fields, error codes: one pm.test per thing the requirement promises, generated rather than hand-typed.
  • Requests are named after the cases. A red assertion in Newman maps to a row in the Excel file without a lookup.
  • No endpoints in the spec, no collection. Casely asks for the API docs instead of guessing a path that 404s on the first run.

Run it in the Collection Runner, or in CI:

newman run exports/casely_api_collection.postman_collection.json \
  -e exports/casely_api_environment.postman_environment.json \
  --env-var "authToken=<token from your CI secret store>"

Install

claude.ai, Cowork, and the Claude desktop app

Install Casely from Anthropic's plugin directory in one click. Claude keeps it updated, and it syncs to Claude Code on the same account.

Claude Code

Paste this prompt and Claude runs the install:

Install the Casely plugin from https://github.com/JohnWayneeee/casely-qa-skill

Or install it as a plugin yourself, which also gets you updates with claude plugin update:

claude plugin marketplace add JohnWayneeee/casely-qa-skill
claude plugin install casely@casely

Or add just the skill to a project:

bunx skills add JohnWayneeee/casely-qa-skill
# or: npx skills@latest add JohnWayneeee/casely-qa-skill

Codex

Codex reads the same plugin manifest:

codex plugin marketplace add JohnWayneeee/casely-qa-skill
codex plugin add casely@casely

Upload the zip by hand (only if the plugin directory is not available to you)

  1. Get the upload archive, already zipped with casely/ at its root: download casely-vX.Y.Z.zip from the latest release.

    Building it yourself works too, but not with GitHub's own "Download ZIP" button: it wraps everything in casely-qa-skill-main/skills/casely/ instead of putting SKILL.md at the archive root, which is what claude.ai requires:

    git clone https://github.com/JohnWayneeee/casely-qa-skill.git
cd casely-qa-skill/skills && zip -r casely.zip casely

  2. On claude.ai, open Settings → Capabilities, turn on Code execution if it isn't already, then go to Skills → Create skill and upload the zip.

  3. The Claude desktop app uses the same account, so the skill is available there too, with nothing to install separately.

  4. Start a chat, attach your files, describe what you need.

Nothing to install locally. The export step uses openpyxl, which already ships inside Claude's code execution environment. Custom skills are private to your account (Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan required) and won't sync to a Claude Code install. Set that up separately with the command above.

Pick Opus. The plan phase decides what gets tested at all: which boundaries matter, which conditions combine, which requirement is too vague to test. Smaller models write acceptable cases from a plan they were handed, and miss the holes in the spec.

What you get

  • exports/all_test_cases.xlsx with one row per case and your own column headers. Import it once instead of forty times. Ask for CSV and you also get all_test_cases.csv.
  • results/*.md, one file per case, so you can review or version-control them separately.
  • A Postman collection, an environment file and run instructions when the requirements describe an API, with every base URL, token and id already pulled out into variables.
  • A list of holes in the spec: contradictions, untestable wording ("should be fast"), and error paths the requirements never mention.
  • run/run_report.md after /casely:run: pass, fail or blocked per UI case, with a screenshot for every failure.
  • bugs/*.md after /casely:bug: one bug report per trace ID or failed case, in your team's fields, with personal data masked.

The export refuses to write a file it cannot read faithfully. A case that reaches TestRail without its steps costs more than a failed export, so malformed input gets named and fixed before delivery.

FAQ

Do I need to run commands?

No. Attach the files, describe what you need, and answer when Casely asks which module to cover. The one place it pauses is the test plan.

Can I use my team's own Excel columns?

That is the point. Attach an existing test case file and Casely copies the headers, their order and the writing style. No config file. Say yes when it offers to save the style, and the next conversation needs no example.

Does it work with Russian requirements?

Yes. Casely writes the cases in the language of your examples.

Which test management systems can import the output?

Any tool that reads Excel: TestRail, Qase, Zephyr, Xray. The columns match whatever your team already uses.

Can it produce API tests I can actually run?

Yes, when the requirements name endpoints. Casely says in the plan how many cases are API-level, and after your approval it exports them as a Postman collection with an environment file and a README. Base URL, tokens and entity ids are variables you fill in once; nothing is hardcoded, and no credential ever lands in the file. Run it in Postman or with Newman in CI. If the spec only describes screens and flows, Casely asks for the API docs rather than inventing endpoints.

Is there a free AI test case generator?

Casely is free and open-source under the MIT license. You pay only for the Claude or Codex plan you already use.

Can I import AI-generated test cases into TestRail?

Yes. Casely exports one .xlsx with your team's column headers, so the TestRail Excel/CSV import maps it in a single pass. The same file works for Qase, Zephyr and Xray.

What about scanned PDFs?

Text-based PDFs, DOCX and XLSX work well. An image-only scan with no selectable text may not extract cleanly, so export a text version when you can.

Project structure

casely-qa-skill/
├── .claude-plugin/          # plugin + marketplace manifests (Claude Code, Codex)
├── .mcp.json                # Atlassian remote MCP (Jira, Confluence), OAuth sign-in
├── commands/run.md          # /casely:run, walks the cases in a browser via Playwright MCP
├── commands/bug.md          # /casely:bug, bug report from a trace ID, logs or a failed case
├── tests/                   # export round-trip test (Arabic, Korean, CSV, XLSX)
├── skills/casely/
│   ├── SKILL.md               # the skill definition and workflow
│   ├── scripts/
│   │   ├── export_to_xlsx.py            # Markdown → Excel (and CSV) exporter
│   │   └── build_postman_collection.py  # API cases → Postman collection
│   ├── references/            # test design, style, saved style, connectors, export, API
│   └── evals/                 # evaluation cases
├── benchmark/                # sample spec + team style file, and a scoring rubric
└── docs/hosted-web-version.md

This skill runs inside your AI assistant. If your team wants a browser UI, file uploads and a review flow with no setup, join the early access list at casely.digital.
